experiment: DCF-21 generalisation of escalate-on-abstention to the DCF-14 graph families
generator: DCF-14 width14.run_instance (gen.py families, all operators, independent exact verification) with fresh seeds
policy: escalate: BP at the budget; act if BP acts; if BP abstains or cannot run, the cheapest exact operator whose ops plus BP's fit the budget, else abstain; no tunable parameter
baselines: exact_else_mbe (DCF-14 strongest hand policy, selected on DCF-14 development data)
objective: verified expected utility - lambda * ops / 2^B, averaged per condition (family, n, budget, penalty); only verified instances
lambda_note: 0.05 is DCF-14's own label weight; 0.2 and 0.5 are declared here as higher compute prices

gates.F1: BP abstention captures at least 80% of the decisions where BP and the verified exact posterior disagree (pooled over verified instances, budgets where BP ran, both penalties)
gates.E1: at lambda 0.05, escalate beats exact_else_mbe in more conditions than it loses
gates.E2: at some declared lambda, escalate beats the best of all other policies (abstain included), chosen per condition with hindsight, in more conditions than it loses

secondary: DCF-16 held-out records (already used for the EvalMath baseline): escalate vs the EvalMath symbolic predictor vs always-BP, expected utility and mean ops; descriptive only
